headline: Panthers' Sandis Vilmanis exits game after hit by Capitals' Tom Wilson
take:
ESPN reports Panthers forward Sandis Vilmanis left the game after a hit from Capitals forward Tom Wilson, who drew a major penalty for boarding and a game misconduct. The report says Vilmanis was shaken up and doesn't say whether he'll miss time.

If he does, Florida loses a depth winger who has been better than his box score. Vilmanis has 3 goals and 7 points in 15 games so far this season, but the Panthers have controlled 63% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice at 5-on-5, and the team's share runs about 13 points better with him in the lineup. That is a strong mark for 13 minutes a night. FLA is 9-5-2 and, as a team, has created slightly more than it has allowed (53.6% of expected goals), so one fourth-line absence won't change much. Wilson's own season is the other story: 2 goals against about 5 expected so far this season, which looks more like bad finishing than a drop in play. We can't say who would pick up Vilmanis's minutes, since our data has no projection for that.
